name: Approval without vote
title: RECOMMENDATION FOR SECOND READING on the Council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a directive of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Directive (EU) 2025/… as regards certain driving disqualifications
part_text:
The European Parliament has approved a new European Union law on driving bans. If a driver is banned from driving for a serious offence in one European Union country, that ban will now be shared and recognised across the Union. The serious offences covered include drink or drug driving, extreme speeding, and driving that causes death or serious injury. Today drivers often escape punishment when they commit these offences outside the country that issued their licence. The aim is to end that impunity and make roads safer.

- **What changes:** Driving bans for serious offences will be shared and recognised between European Union countries.
- **Who it affects:** Drivers banned for drink or drug driving, extreme speeding, or causing death or serious injury abroad.
- **What happens next:** The act is adopted; it will be signed and published in the Official Journal.
